Proves AR-6's `gt` (ordering) operator on a `decimal` field — the second half of AR-7's `decimal` coverage (046 covers `eq`), showing the numeric-string representation survives an ordering comparison as well, not just equality. As with 046, the wire value (`49.95`, a plain JS number — AG Grid's number filter has no distinct decimal wire shape) is coerced by the adapter into a `decimalValue` (`{"type":"decimal","value":"49.95"}`) using the field's schema-declared `decimal` type (SEM-5). Postgres binds the numeric string as a parameter against the `numeric` column; MongoDB uses `$numberDecimal` Extended JSON; OpenSearch/Elasticsearch represents it as a plain JSON number in a `range` query — the same documented, accepted ES precision-limited divergence noted in 046's description.md, since the pinned 7.10-era subset has no arbitrary-precision decimal type.
